A hash table is a data structure that implements an associative array abstract data type, a structure that can map keys to values. Hash tables use a hash function to compute an index into an array of buckets or slots, from which the desired value can be found. However, due to the nature of hash functions, there can be situations where different keys hash to the same index, leading to a collision. Various strategies can be employed to handle these collisions, including separate chaining, open addressing, and more.
